featured_reviews.review_text:
Masta chamchamit is exactly like it’s name. Here you can taste the actual maharashtrian homemade seafood.

Their service is also really good. Cleanliness has been maintained. So if you’re in Dadar/prabhadevi/ worali area let this be your next spot for all your seafood cravings.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently had the pleasure of trying the offerings from this small setup food stall, and I must say, they are off to a fantastic start! The highlight for me was the crab curry—it was absolutely amazing. The flavors were rich, perfectly balanced, and the crab was cooked to perfection, making every bite a delight.

What makes this experience even more special is the homemade touch in every dish. The food feels fresh, comforting, and authentic, as if made with love in a family kitchen. The fish dishes were equally impressive, with fresh ingredients and well-balanced spices that made the flavors truly stand out.

If you’re looking for fresh, flavorful, homemade seafood, especially a standout crab curry, this is a startup worth supporting. I’ll definitely be coming back for more!

We visited Nude Food Café as a group of five and, unfortunately, the experience didn’t go as well as we hoped. Although we were told the wait would be around 20 minutes, we ended up waiting 1.5 hours for a table, while others seemed to be seated much faster. The staff and owners were polite, but the communication about wait times needs improvement, and there were no proper waiting arrangements.

On the positive side, the café has a great eco-friendly concept with a zero-waste food policy, which I really appreciate. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, even though the space feels a bit small and crowded.

The coffee was excellent, the chicken pie was tasty (could’ve used a spicy note), and the pasta dishes were nice, though one was slightly undercooked and could have used more spice. Portions felt a bit small for the price.

Overall, while the café’s concept and ambience are lovely, the extremely slow service and long wait time took away from the experience. Expanding the seating area or managing reservations more clearly would help a lot.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Title: A Momo Lover's Paradise: Delicious Momos at Affordable Prices

Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)

If you're a fan of momos and happen to be in the Century Bazaar area, look no further than this hidden gem located opposite Croma. This place, with its delectable momos, is a must-visit for any momo enthusiast.

The menu at this momo joint offers a variety of options, and we had the pleasure of trying the steam chicken and paneer momos. Both variations were outstanding. The momos were perfectly cooked, with a tender filling and a delicate, well-seasoned outer layer. It was evident that they were made with care and attention to detail.

What impressed me even more was the reasonable pricing. For just Rs. 60, we enjoyed a half-plate of steam momos, with all the variations available. If you prefer fried momos, they offer the same deal at Rs. 70. The affordability coupled with the excellent quality of the momos makes this place a winner.

To elevate the taste of the momos, they provide a delectable combination of sauces and mayonnaise. The sauces complemented the momos perfectly, enhancing their flavors and adding an extra zing to each bite. It was a delicious culinary experience.

The ambiance of the place is ideal for a fun evening with friends. It's always bustling with people, which is a testament to the popularity of the food they serve. The lively atmosphere and the aroma of freshly cooked momos create a welcoming and enjoyable environment.

In conclusion, if you're in the mood for some mouthwatering momos at pocket-friendly prices, this place is a must-visit. With its wide variety of options, excellent taste, and friendly atmosphere, it's the perfect spot to satisfy your momo cravings. Just be prepared for a crowd, as this place has earned a well-deserved reputation among food lovers.

Ashok Vada Pav near Kirti College, Dadar definitely attracts a huge crowd. We reached around 2:15 PM and still had to wait close to 40 minutes in the queue before getting served, which itself shows how popular the place is.

The location is definitely a plus point since it’s close to Dadar Beach. The highlight for me was the crispy chura, which added a unique crunch and gave the vada pav a different texture compared to regular stalls.

However, the overall experience felt a bit overrated for the wait and pricing. The service was slow, there was no extra chutney or extra chura provided, and the vada pavs were simply wrapped in paper and handed over. Since everything is pre-made, there’s almost no scope for customization in terms of chutney or spice level like you usually get at local vendors. Personally, I also found the taste slightly too sweet.

The pricing is ₹35 for a single vada pav and ₹140 for four pieces, which feels almost double compared to many other local vendors offering similar or even better taste.

Overall, it’s worth trying once for the hype and experience, but personally I don’t think the taste and service justify waiting more than 40 minutes when there are plenty of local places serving equally good vada pav with faster service, better customization, and more value for money.

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
In a city that runs on speed, spice, and soul, some places don’t just serve food, they become emotion. Ashok Vada Pav near Kirti College is exactly that kind of institution, where generations have stood shoulder to shoulder, waiting for that one perfect bite.
What makes their vada pav truly iconic is the balance. The batata vada is crisp on the outside, soft and flavourful inside, with just the right hint of garlic and spice. The pav is always fresh, lightly toasted, and acts as the perfect carrier without overpowering the star.
But the real magic lies in their chutney game. That signature dry garlic chutney hits instantly with a bold, smoky spice, while the fried green chillies on the side elevate the entire experience. It’s not just heat, it’s character, the kind that lingers and keeps you coming back.
And then comes the cult favourite, the chura pav. Buttery, spicy, slightly messy, and absolutely addictive. The crushed vada mixed with chutneys and masala, soaked into the pav, creates a texture and flavour bomb that feels indulgent in the most Mumbai way possible. Crisp edges, soft centres, and that unmistakable street-style richness.
Being a true Dadarkar, I’ve grown up eating this vada pav, and what’s incredible is how the taste has remained exactly the same over the years, still the best vada pav, hands down.
There’s a legacy here that you can actually taste. Started decades ago and now run by the next generation, Ashok Vada Pav has become a landmark in Dadar’s food scene. It has seen college crowds, office rush, late-night hunger, and everything in between, yet the consistency remains untouched. No unnecessary reinvention, just doing the basics exceptionally well, every single time. The vibe is classic Mumbai, fast-moving queues, minimal waiting despite the crowd, and an energy that feels alive. You don’t come here for luxury, you come here for authenticity.
Ashok Vada Pav isn’t just food, it’s a ritual, a memory, and for many, a weekly craving that never fades.
Simple, iconic, and absolutely unbeatable. 🌶️🔥

featured_reviews.name: Roshani Batra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Chai Pe Charcha is one of those places that instantly feels cozy the moment you step in. It’s not just about chai here — it’s about conversations, comfort food, and even some fun with their collection of board games.

I tried two of their teas — the adrak chai and the kesar chai. The adrak chai had that strong, gingery warmth that wakes you up and feels like home. The kesar chai, on the other hand, was fragrant, creamy, and felt like a little indulgence in a cup. Both were perfectly brewed and served piping hot.

On the food side, the cheese Maggi was pure nostalgia — gooey, cheesy, and super comforting. But the star for me was the paneer bhurji with paratha. The paneer was soft and well-spiced, and the paratha paired beautifully with it — simple, hearty, and satisfying.

What I loved most though is the vibe of the place. It’s laid-back, student-friendly, and the board games make it a fun spot to spend time with friends while sipping chai. Prices are pocket-friendly too, which makes it even better.

If you’re a chai lover looking for a hangout spot that blends good food, great tea, and a chill atmosphere — this place should definitely be on your list!

featured_reviews.name: Vidyadheesh Upadhye
featured_reviews.review_text:
This review is for a delivery experience with this restaurant.

This place has decent reviews from its customers and hence decided to order from here. The ordering process was navigated smoothly and got a confirmation within 2 minutes regarding acceptance of the order. The order was delivered well within the promoised timelines.

I had ordered the following from their kitchen:

ONION KULCHA [INR 40]
Coarsely chopped onions which were tossed in oil, were patted on top of a refined flour [Maida] Kulcha. Frankly, it didn’t seem like a Kulcha to me, it was a Naan; since Kulcha dough has to be essentially kept aside and allowed to rise. Also the fact that the filling was not stuffed inside the Kulcha but patted on the surface didn’t make sense to me.
It was very rubbery in feel &ntexture as well.

GOBHI KULCHA [INR 50]
This Kulcha was also prepared in the same manner as Onion Kulcha; hence it didn’t curry any favour with me.

ALU MUTTER [INR 145]
This was the most decent preparation of my order though it was made excessively oily. The flavor of the spices and onions used in the gravy was spot-on, the peas were cooked properly yet whole and chunks of boiled potatoes added bulk to the whole dish. When such dishes come my way, I hold a lid on top of the container and tilt it to drain away the excess oil or use a slice of bread to absorb it.

I will try ordering again from here though I have reason for doing so.

featured_reviews.name: Neiladri Chakravarty
featured_reviews.review_text:
This might be the best seated roadside stall ever. Get the keema pav, kulcha, kaleji fry, whatever honesty, it's all good. It's run in front of a home and the service is incredibly fast. You order, sit down and within 5 minutes, your whole steaming dinner is in front of you. Sometimes the uncle forgets one dish because of the insane number of orders pouring in, but you remind him and he serves it to you with a warm smile.

It's got a makeshift seating arrangement on the side of the road, and an elevated surface to eat as well. The eating experience might not be to everyone's liking due to the sheer openness of the place, but I liked the homely communal vibe!

Do not forget to eat at Reva's if you're in Dadar. Just remember that they don't operate every day: select few nights, from 8 to 10.30 ish (?).
